questions.question: how do i run a full rebuild of the api search index?

questions.question: customer says their refund never showed up. how do i trace it through the logs?

claims.claim: Never search for card numbers in logs as they are never logged and searching for card-like regexes triggers internal security audits.
Narrow the search window in the log search tool to a specific 2- to 4-hour window around the cancellation or support ticket.
A normal refund lifecycle in the payments service produces three distinct log lines in index sorrel-prod-*: 'refund requested', 'refund sent', and 'refund settled'.
To locate the payment reference (ref) from a booking_id, search the sorrel-prod-* index with `service=payments booking_id="<booking_id>"`, find the 'refund requested' line, and copy the ref value.
To trace outbound dispatch to stripe, run `service=payments msg="refund sent" ref="<ref>"` to see when the instruction reached stripe and inspect the HTTP response status.

If 'refund sent' returned HTTP 200, Stripe acknowledged the instruction; if HTTP 4xx/5xx, check provider_ms, provider error messages, and status.stripe.com; if no result is found, check for queue deadlocks or database issues.
To check webhook settlement, run `service=payments msg="refund settled" ref="<ref>"`.
If the 'refund settled' line exists, the cycle is complete, and any delay is due to inter-bank processing delays (typically 5–10 business days).

If no 'refund settled' line appears, it is normal if 'refund sent' was fewer than 6 hours ago; otherwise check webhook health on the Sorrel / payments dashboard or query `service=payments msg="webhook" outcome=retry ref="<ref>"`.
If one reference shows two 'sent' lines, money may have moved twice: stop the investigation immediately and page Mei.
